$comment: What a trip is made of: the fields, the stages they belong to, and what
each goal cannot be done without.
Data rather than code because two implementations read it. It was a literal
inside the TypeScript model, which was fine while there was one; a second
copy in Python would have been a table that drifts silently, and the drift
would show up as an agent that asks for something it already has.
Generated from the TypeScript model's golden the first time; the golden

fields.label: where you are going
fields.note: City or airport. Everything else is priced against it.

fields.label: which airport you are flying from
fields.note: Three-letter code. Never assumed — suggested from the browser, confirmed by the traveler.

fields.label: when you are leaving
fields.note: YYYY-MM-DD. No fare is real without it.

fields.label: when you are coming back
fields.note: YYYY-MM-DD. With startDate it gives the number of nights.

fields.label: how many of you are going
fields.note: Adults and older children — everyone needing a seat and a bed.

fields.label: which cabin
fields.note: Defaults to economy when nobody says otherwise.

fields.label: whether to exclude connections
fields.note: A preference, not a requirement: it filters the search.

fields.label: the most you would pay per seat
fields.note: Per traveler, one way. Filters the search rather than the display.

fields.label: the flight you chose
fields.note: The id from the card they tapped. Its fare feeds the total.

fields.label: what that flight costs
fields.note: Per traveler. Saved alongside the id so the total is theirs, not an average.

fields.label: which part of town
fields.note: Narrows the stays that come back.

fields.label: the most per night
fields.note: Filters stays. Distinct from the trip budget.

fields.label: where you are staying
fields.note: The id from the card they tapped.

fields.label: what that stay costs a night
fields.note: Saved with the id, for the same reason as flightPrice.

fields.label: what the whole trip should come to
fields.note: All in, for everyone. What the progress meter measures against.

fields.label: what is committed so far
fields.note: Booked, not estimated.

fields.label: anything else worth remembering
fields.note: One line. Preferences and constraints that do not have a field.

fields.label: a day-by-day plan
fields.note: Set once the itinerary has been drawn and the traveler is happy with it.

fields.label: the parts that do not apply
fields.note: Stages this trip does not need — driving rather than flying, staying with family, no fixed budget. A skipped stage counts as settled and is never asked about again.

fields.label: the values nobody confirmed
fields.note: Fields filled in without being told. They pre-fill controls but do not settle a stage, so the traveler is still asked.

fields.label: the other stops
fields.note: Additional stops beyond the first, each with its own dates. The flat fields describe the first leg; this is how a two-city trip stops being two half-described trips.
